recommendation: Keep this audit as-is. Do not add redundant Subscription prose or a core default-message element for FHIR-18992 without a new work-group decision; any future SMS channel or standardized default-message extension should be handled as a separate current-scope proposal.
issue_request: FHIR-18992 was a Published / Persuasive with Modification STU3 Subscription issue asking that SMS and email subscriptions work better than raw XML/JSON by ensuring text/plain is usable and by explaining intended SMS/email use, while explicitly not adding a core default-message element.
initial_application: Commit f6ab808915 applied GF#18992 by adding old Subscription notes that text/plain can be useful for email and SMS together with an extension describing conversion of resources to text. Related commit 80086b8f22 applied the sibling FHIR-18991 payload datatype/value-set prerequisite.
additional_context: FHIR-18991 is the same 2018 Subscription channel/payload change family. Current R5/R6 topic-based Subscription source remains active in source/fhir.ini, but the core-defined channel list now includes rest-hook, websocket, email, and message, without a current core SMS section. Subscription.contentType is a code required-bound to ValueSet/mimetypes and explicitly notes text/plain/text/html for the Email channel; the Email narrative describes human-readable bodies, text/plain examples, attachment MIME parameters, and non-PHI standard body behavior.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no current source edit is needed: the MimeTypes binding and current Email channel narrative already preserve the implementer-visible outcome of the accepted issue, the default-message element was intentionally not added, and SMS is no longer a core Subscription channel section to update.

related_jiras.note: Changed the Subscription payload datatype/binding and revised the SMS/email payload note that FHIR-18992 depended on.
